reconstructed_theorem_text: Let X be a measurable space, let mu be a nonzero sigma-finite measure on X, and let f,g : X -> R. Assume that f is measurable, x |-> exp(f(x)) and x |-> exp(g(x)) are mu-integrable, and r : X -> R defined by r(x) = f(x) - log(integral_X exp(f) dmu) - g(x) + log(integral_X exp(g) dmu) is integrable with respect to mu.tilted f. Then klDiv(mu.tilted f, mu.tilted g) != infinity, and toReal(klDiv(mu.tilted f, mu.tilted g)) = integral_X r d(mu.tilted f).
objects: X; mu; f; g; r; mu.tilted f; mu.tilted g; klDiv(mu.tilted f, mu.tilted g).
domains: X is a measurable space; mu is a measure on X; f, g, and r are functions X -> R; mu.tilted f and mu.tilted g are probability measures on X; klDiv(mu.tilted f, mu.tilted g) is extended-nonnegative-real valued.
quantifiers: Universally quantified over X, its measurable-space structure, mu, f, and g; r is locally defined from them.
assumptions: mu is nonzero and sigma-finite; f is measurable; exp(f) and exp(g) are mu-integrable; r is integrable with respect to mu.tilted f.
conclusion: klDiv(mu.tilted f, mu.tilted g) is not infinity, and its toReal value equals the integral of r with respect to mu.tilted f.
scopes: Both normalized tilts use the same base measure mu. The integrability assumption and concluding integral for r are under the left tilt mu.tilted f. The two normalizing integrals are under mu. The finiteness certificate and toReal equality are jointly asserted.
constant_dependencies: There is no universal numerical constant. Each tilt depends on the common base measure mu and its own potential; r depends on f, g, and both logarithmic normalizing integrals.
